sanskrit: tasmād adya sthiro bhūtvā jñātvā lokasya nirṇayam śṛṇu yuddhaṃ yathā vṛttaṃ ghoraṃ devāsuropamam
english: Therefore now, holding yourself steady and grasping the world's appointed end, hear how the battle was waged—terrible, like the war of gods and demons.

sanskrit: praviṣṭe tava sainyaṃ tu śaineye satyavikrame bhīmasenamukhāḥ pārthāḥ pratīyur vāhinīṃ tava
english: When the Śaineya of true valor had entered your army, the sons of Pṛthā with Bhīmasena at their head advanced against your host.

sanskrit: āgacchatas tān sahasā kruddharūpān sahānugān dadhāraiko raṇe pāṇḍūn kṛtavarmā mahārathaḥ
english: As they came on suddenly, wrathful in aspect and with their followers, Kṛtavarman the great chariot-warrior alone held back the Pāṇḍavas in battle.

sanskrit: yathodvṛttaṃ dhārayate velā vai salilārṇavam pāṇḍusainyaṃ tathā saṃkhye hārdikyaḥ samavārayat
english: As the shore holds back the surging ocean of waters, so in the fray did the son of Hṛdika hold back the Pāṇḍava army.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam amanyanta hārdikyasya parākramam yad enaṃ sahitāḥ pārthā nāticakramur āhave
english: There they deemed it a marvel, the prowess of the son of Hṛdika, that the sons of Pṛthā united could not overpass him in the battle.

sanskrit: tato bhīmas tribhir viddhvā kṛtavarmāṇam āyasaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau mahābāhur harṣayan sarvapāṇḍavān
english: Then Bhīma, having pierced Kṛtavarman with three iron shafts, the mighty-armed one blew his conch, gladdening all the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: sahadevas tu viṃśatyā dharmarājaś ca pañcabhiḥ śatena nakulaś cāpi hārdikyaṃ samavidhyata
english: Sahadeva with twenty, the King of Righteousness with five, and Nakula too with a hundred shafts pierced the son of Hṛdika.

sanskrit: draupadeyās trisaptatyā saptabhiś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnas tribhiś cāpi kṛtavarmāṇam ārdayat virāṭo drupadaś caiva yājñaseniś ca pañcabhiḥ
english: The sons of Draupadī with seventy-three, Ghaṭotkaca with seven, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna with three afflicted Kṛtavarman; Virāṭa and Drupada, and the son of Yājñasenī, each with five.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī cāpi hārdikyaṃ viddhvā pañcabhir āśugaiḥ punar vivyādha viṃśatyā sāyakānāṃ hasann iva
english: And Śikhaṇḍin too, having pierced the son of Hṛdika with five swift arrows, struck him again with twenty shafts, as though laughing.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā tato rājan sarvatas tān mahārathān ekaikaṃ pañcabhir viddhvā bhīmaṃ vivyādha saptabhiḥ dhanur dhvajaṃ ca saṃyatto rathād bhūmāv apātayat
english: Then, O King, Kṛtavarman, piercing each one of those great chariot-warriors all about with five shafts apiece, struck Bhīma with seven; and, intent, he cast his bow and his banner from the chariot down to the earth.

sanskrit: athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ tvaramāṇo mahārathaḥ ājaghānorasi kruddhaḥ saptatyā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then upon him whose bow was severed, the great chariot-warrior in haste and wrath struck him on the chest with seventy sharpened shafts.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddho balavān hārdikyasya śarottamaiḥ cacāla rathamadhyasthaḥ kṣitikampe yathācalaḥ
english: Deeply wounded by the son of Hṛdika's finest shafts, the mighty one, standing in the midst of his chariot, swayed like a mountain in an earthquake.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā dharmarājapurogamāḥ visṛjantaḥ śarān ghorān kṛtavarmāṇam ārdayan
english: Seeing Bhīmasena thus, those led by the King of Righteousness, loosing terrible shafts, afflicted Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā koṣṭhakīkṛtya rathavaṃśena māriṣa vivyadhuḥ sāyakair hṛṣṭā rakṣārthaṃ māruter mṛdhe
english: Having thus penned him in with a wall of chariots, O honored one, they joyfully pierced him with shafts to protect the son of the Wind-god in the fray.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ śaktiṃ jagrāha samare hemadaṇḍām ayasmayīm cikṣepa ca rathāt tūrṇaṃ kṛtavarmarathaṃ prati
english: Then, having regained his senses, Bhīmasena of mighty strength seized in battle a golden-shafted iron spear and swiftly hurled it from his chariot at the chariot of Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: sā bhīmabhujanirmuktā nirmuktoragasaṃnibhā kṛtavarmāṇam abhitaḥ prajajvāla sudāruṇā
english: Released from Bhīma's arm, like a serpent that has cast its slough, dreadful, it blazed up all about Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā yugāntāgnisamaprabhām dvābhyāṃ śarābhyāṃ hārdikyo nicakarta dvidhā tadā
english: As it fell suddenly upon him, gleaming like the fire at the end of an age, the son of Hṛdika then cut it in two with a pair of shafts.

sanskrit: sā chinnā patitā bhūmau śaktiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇā dyotayantī diśo rājan maholkeva divaś cyutā śaktiṃ vinihatāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmaś cukrodha vai bhṛśam
english: Severed, the gold-adorned spear fell to the earth, lighting up the quarters, O King, like a great meteor fallen from the sky; and seeing the spear struck down, Bhīma grew exceedingly wrathful.

sanskrit: tato 'nyad dhanur ādāya vegavat sumahāsvanam bhīmaseno raṇe kruddho hārdikyaṃ samavārayat
english: Then, taking up another bow, swift and of mighty twang, Bhīmasena, wrathful in the battle, beset the son of Hṛdika.

sanskrit: athainaṃ pañcabhir bāṇair ājaghāna stanāntare bhīmo bhīmabalo rājaṃs tava durmantritena ha
english: Then Bhīma of terrible strength struck him with five arrows between the breasts, O King—and all by your ill counsel.

sanskrit: bhojas tu kṣatasarvāṅgo bhīmasenena māriṣa raktāśoka ivotphullo vyabhrājata raṇājire
english: The Bhoja, every limb wounded by Bhīmasena, O honored one, shone upon the field of battle like a red aśoka tree in full bloom.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddhas tribhir bāṇair bhīmasenaṃ hasann iva abhihatya dṛḍhaṃ yuddhe tān sarvān pratyavidhyata
english: Then in wrath, as though laughing, he struck Bhīmasena hard with three arrows in the fight, and shot back at all of them.

sanskrit: tribhis tribhir maheṣvāso yatamānān mahārathān te 'pi taṃ pratyavidhyanta saptabhiḥ saptabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: The mighty archer struck those striving great chariot-warriors with three shafts each, and they in turn pierced him back with seven shafts apiece.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinas tataḥ kruddhaḥ kṣurapreṇa mahārathaḥ dhanuś ciccheda samare prahasann iva bhārata
english: Then the great chariot-warrior, wrathful, with a razor-tipped shaft cut Śikhaṇḍin's bow in the battle, as though laughing, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu tataḥ kruddhaś chinne dhanuṣi satvaram asiṃ jagrāha samare śatacandraṃ ca bhāsvaram
english: Then Śikhaṇḍin, wrathful at his bow being cut, quickly seized in the battle a sword and a gleaming hundred-mooned shield.

sanskrit: bhrāmayitvā mahācarma cāmīkaravibhūṣitam tam asiṃ preṣayām āsa kṛtavarmarathaṃ prati
english: Whirling his great gold-adorned shield, he sent that sword flying toward the chariot of Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: sa tasya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ chittvā saṃkhye mahān asiḥ abhyagād dharaṇīṃ rājaṃś cyutaṃ jyotir ivāmbarāt
english: That great sword, having cut his bow together with the arrow upon it in the fray, fell to the earth, O King, like a star fallen from the heavens.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu tvaramāṇā mahārathāḥ vivyadhuḥ sāyakair gāḍhaṃ kṛtavarmāṇam āhave
english: At that very moment the great chariot-warriors, hastening, pierced Kṛtavarman deeply with shafts in the battle.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya tyaktvā tac ca mahad dhanuḥ viśīrṇaṃ bharataśreṣṭha hārdikyaḥ paravīrahā
english: Then, casting aside that great shattered bow and taking up another, the son of Hṛdika, slayer of enemy heroes, O best of the Bharatas,

sanskrit: vivyādha pāṇḍavān yuddhe tribhis tribhir ajihmagaiḥ śikhaṇḍinaṃ ca vivyādha tribhiḥ pañcabhir eva ca
english: pierced the Pāṇḍavas in the fight with three straight-flying shafts each, and pierced Śikhaṇḍin with three and then with five.

sanskrit: dhanur anyat samādāya śikhaṇḍī tu mahāyaśāḥ avārayat kūrmanakhair āśugair hṛdikātmajam
english: But Śikhaṇḍin of great renown, taking up another bow, held back the son of Hṛdika with swift tortoise-nailed shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho raṇe rājan hṛdikasyātmasaṃbhavaḥ abhidudrāva vegena yājñaseniṃ mahāratham
english: Then, wrathful in the battle, O King, the son sprung from Hṛdika rushed swiftly upon the son of Yājñasenī, that great chariot-warrior,

sanskrit: bhīṣmasya samare rājan mṛtyor hetuṃ mahātmanaḥ vidarśayan balaṃ śūraḥ śārdūla iva kuñjaram
english: upon him who in battle was the cause of high-souled Bhīṣma's death, O King—the hero displaying his strength like a tiger against an elephant.

sanskrit: tau diśāgajasaṃkāśau jvalitāv iva pāvakau samāsedatur anyonyaṃ śarasaṃghair ariṃdamau
english: Those two, like the elephants of the quarters, blazing like flames, those two tamers of foes, closed upon each other with masses of arrows.

sanskrit: vidhunvānau dhanuḥśreṣṭhe saṃdadhānau ca sāyakān visṛjantau ca śataśo gabhastīn iva bhāskarau
english: Shaking their splendid bows, nocking their shafts, and loosing them by the hundred like two suns sending forth their rays,

sanskrit: tāpayantau śarais tīkṣṇair anyonyaṃ tau mahārathau yugāntapratimau vīrau rejatur bhāskarāv iva
english: scorching each other with sharp shafts, those two great chariot-warriors, those heroes like the end of an age, shone like two suns.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā tu rabhasaṃ yājñaseniṃ mahāratham viddhveṣūṇāṃ trisaptatyā punar vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: But Kṛtavarman, fiercely piercing the son of Yājñasenī, that great chariot-warrior, with seventy-three arrows, struck him again with seven.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddho vyathito rathopastha upāviśat visṛjan saśaraṃ cāpaṃ mūrchayābhipariplutaḥ
english: Deeply wounded and distressed, he sank down upon the floor of his chariot, letting fall his bow with its arrow, overwhelmed by a swoon.

sanskrit: taṃ viṣaṇṇaṃ rathe dṛṣṭvā tāvakā bharatarṣabha hārdikyaṃ pūjayām āsur vāsāṃsy ādudhuvuś ca ha
english: Seeing him sunk down in his chariot, your men, O bull of the Bharatas, honored the son of Hṛdika and waved their garments aloft.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ tathā jñātvā hārdikyaśarapīḍitam apovāha raṇād yantā tvaramāṇo mahāratham
english: Knowing Śikhaṇḍin thus tormented by the son of Hṛdika's shafts, his charioteer in haste bore the great chariot-warrior away from the battle.

sanskrit: sāditaṃ tu rathopasthe dṛṣṭvā pārthāḥ śikhaṇḍinam parivavrū rathais tūrṇaṃ kṛtavarmāṇam āhave
english: But seeing Śikhaṇḍin laid low upon the floor of his chariot, the sons of Pṛthā swiftly hemmed in Kṛtavarman with their chariots in the battle.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutaṃ paraṃ cakre kṛtavarmā mahārathaḥ yad ekaḥ samare pārthān vārayām āsa sānugān
english: There Kṛtavarman the great chariot-warrior wrought a surpassing marvel, in that alone in battle he held back the sons of Pṛthā with their followers.

sanskrit: pārthāñ jitvājayac cedīn pāñcālān sṛñjayān api kekayāṃś ca mahāvīryān kṛtavarmā mahārathaḥ
english: Having vanquished the sons of Pṛthā, Kṛtavarman the great chariot-warrior overcame the Cedis, the Pāñcālas, and the Sṛñjayas too, and the mighty Kekayas.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare hārdikyena sma pāṇḍavāḥ itaś cetaś ca dhāvanto naiva cakrur dhṛtiṃ raṇe
english: The Pāṇḍavas, being struck down in battle by the son of Hṛdika, running this way and that, could find no firmness in the fray.

sanskrit: jitvā pāṇḍusutān yuddhe bhīmasenapurogamān hārdikyaḥ samare 'tiṣṭhad vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ
english: Having vanquished the sons of Pāṇḍu in the fight, those led by Bhīmasena, the son of Hṛdika stood in the battle like a smokeless fire.

sanskrit: te drāvyamāṇāḥ samare hārdikyena mahārathāḥ vimukhāḥ samapadyanta śaravṛṣṭibhir arditāḥ
english: Those great chariot-warriors, driven off in the battle by the son of Hṛdika and afflicted by his showers of arrows, were turned to flight.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇuṣvaikamanā rājan yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi drāvyamāṇe bale tasmin hārdikyena mahātmanā
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear with single mind, O King, that which you ask of me, when that host was being driven off by the high-souled son of Hṛdika.

sanskrit: lajjayāvanate cāpi prahṛṣṭaiś caiva tāvakaiḥ dvīpo ya āsīt pāṇḍūnām agādhe gādham icchatām
english: And while your men rejoiced and the Pāṇḍavas were bowed down with shame, he who had been an island to them as they sought a foothold in fathomless depths—

sanskrit: śrutvā tu ninadaṃ bhīmaṃ tāvakānāṃ mahāhave śaineyas tvarito rājan kṛtavarmāṇam abhyayāt
english: hearing the terrible roar of your men in the great battle, the Śaineya in haste, O King, advanced upon Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā tu hārdikyaḥ śaineyaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ avākirat susaṃkruddhas tato 'krudhyata sātyakiḥ
english: But Kṛtavarman, son of Hṛdika, in great wrath covered the Śaineya with sharpened shafts; thereat Sātyaki grew wrathful.

sanskrit: tataḥ suniśitaṃ bhallaṃ śaineyaḥ kṛtavarmaṇe preṣayām āsa samare śarāṃś ca caturo 'parān
english: Then the Śaineya sent a well-sharpened broad-headed shaft at Kṛtavarman in the battle, and four other arrows besides.

sanskrit: te tasya jaghnire vāhān bhallenāsyācchinad dhanuḥ pṛṣṭharakṣaṃ tathā sūtam avidhyan niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: They slew his horses; with a broad-headed shaft he severed his bow, and he pierced the rear-guard and the charioteer too with sharpened shafts.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ virathaṃ kṛtvā sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ senām asyārdayām āsa śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Then, having made him chariotless, Sātyaki of true valor afflicted his army with smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: sābhajyatātha pṛtanā śaineyaśarapīḍitā tataḥ prāyād vai tvaritaḥ sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ
english: Then that host, tormented by the Śaineya's shafts, broke apart; and Sātyaki of true valor pressed swiftly onward.

sanskrit: śṛṇu rājan yad akarot tava sainyeṣu vīryavān atītya sa mahārāja droṇānīkamahārṇavam
english: Hear, O King, what that valiant one did among your troops, when, O great King, he had passed beyond the great ocean that was Droṇa's host.

sanskrit: parājitya ca saṃhṛṣṭaḥ kṛtavarmāṇam āhave yantāram abravīc chūraḥ śanair yāhīty asaṃbhramam
english: And the hero, gladdened at having vanquished Kṛtavarman in the battle, said calmly and without flurry to his charioteer, "Go on slowly."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu tava tat sainyaṃ rathāśvadvipasaṃkulam padātijanasaṃpūrṇam abravīt sārathiṃ punaḥ
english: But beholding that army of yours, thronged with chariots, horses, and elephants and filled with foot-soldiers, he spoke again to his charioteer:

sanskrit: yad etan meghasaṃkāśaṃ droṇānīkasya savyataḥ sumahat kuñjarānīkaṃ yasya rukmaratho mukham
english: "That vast elephant-division, dark like a cloud, to the left of Droṇa's host, whose front is the warrior of the golden chariot—

sanskrit: ete hi bahavaḥ sūta durnivāryāś ca saṃyuge duryodhanasamādiṣṭā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ rājaputrā maheṣvāsāḥ sarve vikrāntayodhinaḥ
english: these many, O charioteer, are hard to ward off in battle—commanded by Duryodhana, having given up their lives for my sake, princes and mighty archers, all of them warriors of daring valor.

sanskrit: trigartānāṃ rathodārāḥ suvarṇavikṛtadhvajāḥ mām evābhimukhā vīrā yotsyamānā vyavasthitāḥ
english: The noble chariot-warriors of the Trigartas, with banners wrought of gold, those heroes stand drawn up facing me alone, ready to fight.

sanskrit: atra māṃ prāpaya kṣipram aśvāṃś codaya sārathe trigartaiḥ saha yotsyāmi bhāradvājasya paśyataḥ
english: Bring me there quickly; urge on the horses, O charioteer—I shall fight with the Trigartas before the very eyes of the son of Bharadvāja."

sanskrit: tataḥ prāyāc chanaiḥ sūtaḥ sātvatasya mate sthitaḥ rathenādityavarṇena bhāsvareṇa patākinā
english: Then the charioteer, abiding by the Sātvata's wish, advanced slowly with the chariot sun-hued, gleaming, and bannered.

sanskrit: tam ūhuḥ sārather vaśyā valgamānā hayottamāḥ vāyuvegasamāḥ saṃkhye kundendurajataprabhāḥ
english: Obedient to the charioteer, prancing, the excellent horses bore him, swift as the wind in battle, gleaming like jasmine, the moon, and silver.

sanskrit: āpatantaṃ rathaṃ taṃ tu śaṅkhavarṇair hayottamaiḥ parivavrus tataḥ śūrā gajānīkena sarvataḥ kiranto vividhāṃs tīkṣṇān sāyakāṃl laghuvedhinaḥ
english: As that chariot rushed on with its conch-hued excellent horses, the heroes then hemmed it in on every side with an elephant-division, scattering various sharp, swift-piercing shafts.

sanskrit: sātvato 'pi śitair bāṇair gajānīkam ayodhayat parvatān iva varṣeṇa tapānte jalado mahān
english: The Sātvata too with whetted arrows assailed the elephant-division, as a great cloud assails the mountains with rain at the end of the hot season.

sanskrit: vajrāśanisamasparśair vadhyamānāḥ śarair gajāḥ prādravan raṇam utsṛjya śinivīryasamīritaiḥ
english: Struck by arrows whose touch was like the thunderbolt and lightning, sped by the strength of Śini's line, the elephants fled, abandoning the battle.

sanskrit: śīrṇadantā virudhirā bhinnamastakapiṇḍakāḥ viśīrṇakarṇāsyakarā viniyantṛpatākinaḥ
english: Their tusks broken, bleeding, the bony swellings of their heads burst open, ears, mouths, and trunks torn, bereft of drivers and banners,

sanskrit: saṃbhinnavarmaghaṇṭāś ca saṃnikṛttamahādhvajāḥ hatārohā diśo rājan bhejire bhraṣṭakambalāḥ
english: their armor and bells shattered, their great standards cut down, their riders slain and their housings fallen, they fled, O King, in all directions.

sanskrit: ruvanto vividhān rāvāñ jaladopamanisvanāḥ nārācair vatsadantaiś ca sātvatena vidāritāḥ
english: Bellowing manifold cries, with a din like that of clouds, they were torn open by the Sātvata with iron shafts and calf-tooth arrows.

sanskrit: tasmin drute gajānīke jalasaṃdho mahārathaḥ yattaḥ saṃprāpayan nāgaṃ rajatāśvarathaṃ prati
english: When that elephant-division was put to flight, Jalasaṃdha the great chariot-warrior, intent, brought his elephant toward the silver-horsed chariot.

sanskrit: rukmavarṇakaraḥ śūras tapanīyāṅgadaḥ śuciḥ kuṇḍalī mukuṭī śaṅkhī raktacandanarūṣitaḥ
english: The hero, gold-hued of hand, with armlets of refined gold, pure, wearing earrings, a crown, and a conch-armlet, smeared with red sandal,

sanskrit: śirasā dhārayan dīptāṃ tapanīyamayīṃ srajam urasā dhārayan niṣkaṃ kaṇṭhasūtraṃ ca bhāsvaram
english: bearing on his head a blazing garland wrought of refined gold, bearing on his breast a golden ornament and a gleaming neck-chain,

sanskrit: cāpaṃ ca rukmavikṛtaṃ vidhunvan gajamūrdhani aśobhata mahārāja savidyud iva toyadaḥ
english: and brandishing a bow wrought with gold upon the elephant's head, shone, O great King, like a rain-cloud charged with lightning.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā māgadhasya gajottamam sātyakir vārayām āsa velevodvṛttam arṇavam
english: As the Magadha king's noble elephant rushed suddenly on, Sātyaki held it back as the shore holds the surging sea.

sanskrit: nāgaṃ nivāritaṃ dṛṣṭvā śaineyasya śarottamaiḥ akrudhyata raṇe rājañ jalasaṃdho mahābalaḥ
english: Seeing his elephant held back by the Śaineya's finest shafts, Jalasaṃdha of mighty strength grew wrathful in the battle, O King.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho maheṣvāso mārgaṇair bhārasādhanaiḥ avidhyata śineḥ pautraṃ jalasaṃdho mahorasi
english: Then the wrathful mighty archer Jalasaṃdha pierced the grandson of Śini upon the broad chest with shafts that bear a heavy work.

sanskrit: tato 'pareṇa bhallena pītena niśitena ca asyato vṛṣṇivīrasya nicakarta śarāsanam
english: Then with another broad-headed shaft, yellow and sharpened, he cut asunder the bow of the Vṛṣṇi hero as he was shooting.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ prahasann iva bhārata avidhyan māgadho vīraḥ pañcabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: At Sātyaki, whose bow was severed, as though laughing, O Bhārata, the Magadha hero shot, striking him with five sharpened shafts.

sanskrit: sa viddho bahubhir bāṇair jalasaṃdhena vīryavān nākampata mahābāhus tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Though pierced by many arrows from Jalasaṃdha, the valiant, mighty-armed one did not waver—and that was as it were a marvel.

sanskrit: acintayan vai sa śarān nātyarthaṃ saṃbhramād balī dhanur anyat samādāya tiṣṭha tiṣṭhety uvāca ha
english: Heeding the arrows not at all, the mighty one, without much flurry, took up another bow and said, "Stand, stand!"
